title: fetch, JSON and handling network errors

videos.script:
Everything so far has lived inside one program. {{server}} Real pages get their data from a server: the list of books, the user's loans, the result of a search. The way a page asks is fetch, and the answers usually come back as JSON.

{{json}} So first JSON, the text format nearly every API speaks. It looks like a JavaScript object, and it is not one: a date comes back as a string, a Map comes back empty, and nothing tells you.

{{fetch}} Then fetch, against the lab's own small server. Asking is two lines. The lesson is in the failures.

{{surprise}} Here is the first surprise. A request for a book that does not exist, a 404, does not make fetch fail. Neither does a server error, a 500. As far as fetch is concerned, an answer arrived, and that is success. Your code has to check.

{{rest}} Then the failures that are real failures: no connection at all, a server that sends a web page instead of JSON, a server that takes forever and needs a timeout. And retrying, carefully, when a server says try again.
